title: Reorder List
description:
# Reorder List

You are given the head of a singly linked list. If the original node order is:

`L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln-1 -> Ln`

reorder the same nodes into this order:

`L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> L2 -> Ln-2 -> ...`

You may not modify the values stored in the nodes. Only the `next` pointers may be changed. The returned order in the examples is written as an array only to describe the final linked-list order.

Example arrays display values in `next` order; `[]` denotes an empty list (`null`). A node stores its value in `val` and its next node in `next`. Use node objects for list parameters and results as shown in the initial code.

## Example 1:

**Input:** head = [1,2,3,4]
**Output:** [1,4,2,3]

## Example 2:

**Input:** head = [1,2,3,4,5]
**Output:** [1,5,2,4,3]

## Constraints:

*   The number of nodes in the list is in the range `[1, 5 * 10^4]`.
*   `1 <= Node.val <= 1000`

tests.description: Odd-length canonical reorder leaves the middle node last
Three-node list places the tail after the head
Values do not matter; only positions are rearranged
Duplicate values prove the operation is positional
Longer even list checks repeated alternation
Longer odd list checks the final middle node

diagrams.caption: Input list before any next pointers are rearranged

solutions.name: Find Middle + Reverse + Merge
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use slow and fast pointers to find the end of the first half. Cut the list there, reverse the second half in place, then merge the two halves by alternating one node from the first half and one node from the reversed second half.

## Key Insight

The desired order is the original front half interleaved with the back half read from right to left. Reversing the second half turns that right-to-left order into a normal forward traversal.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Deque Front/Back Rebuild
solutions.description:
## Approach

Put every node after the head into a deque. Starting from `head`, alternately take a node from the back and the front of the deque, attach it after the current node, and advance the current pointer.

## Key Insight

The target order repeatedly asks for the farthest remaining tail node, then the nearest remaining front node. A deque exposes exactly those two ends and makes the desired order explicit.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Recursive Front Pointer
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use recursion to walk to the tail while a `front` pointer starts at the head. During the unwind phase, insert the current tail-side node after `front`, then move `front` one step forward. Stop once the two sides meet or cross.

## Key Insight

The call stack naturally visits nodes from the end of the list back toward the middle. Pairing that tail-side visit with a moving front pointer produces the same outside-in order without explicitly reversing a half.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Stack of Second-Half Nodes
solutions.description:
## Approach

Find the middle with slow and fast pointers. Push the nodes after the middle onto a stack, cut the list after the middle, then pop nodes and insert each one after the next node of the first half.

## Key Insight

Only the second half needs to be consumed from back to front. A stack gives that reverse order directly while keeping the first half in its original forward order.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
